newsitem.title: USA: SEC subpoenas developer in Nevada Cty, Calif probe.
newsitem.headline: SEC subpoenas developer in Nevada Cty, Calif probe.

text.p: A former developer linked to failed land deals in California was subpoenaed by the Securities and Exchange Commission as part of its probe of Nevada County, Calif., bonds, his attorney said on Thursday.

G. Michael Montross, who is being held in a San Mateo County, Calif., jail pending a December preliminary hearing on charges of California securities violations, was recently subpoenaed by the SEC to answer questions about the Nevada County bonds, his attorney, David Packard, said.
Montross will meet with the SEC within the next three weeks, but Packard said he would advise his client not to answer the SEC's questions about the Nevada County bonds.
"They (SEC investigators) certainly want to get as much information as they can about the Nevada County bonds," Packard said.
Packard added, however, that "when it comes to substantive questions related to the bonds, he (Montross) will assert the Fifth Amendment."

Packard, who represents Montross in the San Mateo County case, said he believed Montross could be a target of the SEC municipal bond probe in Nevada County, which has focused on the county, underwriter First California Capital Markets Group Inc and other bond professionals involved in the deal.
SEC officials in San Francisco were not immediately available to comment. They have refused comment in the past.

Montross was taken into custody in June after more than two years on the run, authorities said. Before he was moved to San Mateo County, where he is currently being held, Montross served time in Los Angeles for allegedly making false statements on a passport application.

More than two years ago, the San Mateo County District Attorney's office filed 93 counts of state securities violations against Montross related to two failed land developments, including a land deal in Nevada County.
Chuck Finney, deputy district attorney for San Mateo County, said the charges brought by his office against Montross did not involve the Nevada County bonds.

A warrant for Montross's arrest was issued in December 1993. But investigators said they could not find him. In the months that followed, investigators believe Montross traveled around the country, eventually settling in Newport Beach, Calif. Authorities believe Montross was preparing to leave for Costa Rica when he was caught.
Montross has pleaded not guilty to all of the San Mateo County charges, his attorney said.
Packard said he would argue in court that investors knew the "material risk" of the land developments.
Bonds issued by Nevada County and the California cities of Avenal, Ione and Wasco, and underwritten by First California, have been the subject of a lengthy SEC investigation.

The SEC held special meetings in September with several of the targets in the probe, a development that had suggested the SEC may be preparing to act. It was unclear Thursday how a meeting with Montross would impact the SEC probe or its plans.
